incidental_context.reason: LAW:UPDR2_LOAN supplies additional agriculturist restrictions, workman qualifications, excluded lenders and loan exceptions. The permitted controversy specifically concerns agriculturist status, income-tax, property recovery and the advance-date proviso. A separate point for each unlitigated statutory alternative would create unsupported weighting.

EA115 requires an intentional declaration, act or omission causing another party to believe and act on a representation. The reported absence of an initial objection does not establish these elements. P32 records the historical silence; P40 preserves the unresolved procedural effect without requiring an affirmative estoppel or waiver holding.

CPC11 requires the relevant matter to have been directly and substantially in issue and heard and finally decided, subject to its detailed conditions. The High Court did not address the accounting-start issue in the supplied record. The materials do not establish every preclusion element. It would be unwarranted to require a categorical res judicata conclusion.

CPC47 concerns questions of execution, discharge or satisfaction determined by the executing court. The recorded application expressly proceeded under section 8 of the Debt Redemption Act before the decree court. The excerpts do not show that a distinct CPC47 jurisdictional dispute was litigated. P03–P05 and P39 retain the source-grounded statutory framework.

The decree-holders alleged joint Hindu family circumstances, preserved in P17. Neither that pleading nor the presence of sons on the 1931 deed establishes the conditions for CPC53 ancestral-property liability or a separate EA50 relationship-opinion analysis.

The arbitration, lease, partition, contract formation, mistake, damages, governmental finance and constitutional equality excerpts have no established operative relationship to the presented mortgage-decree controversy. In particular LAW:ARB21 concerns arbitration, while the High Court's reported section 21 reference concerns the Debt Redemption Act. These must not be conflated.

reference_uncertainties.detail: S5c8b7a555503 describes the mortgage as securing Rs. 3,000 while also reciting a cheque advance of Rs. 8,000. The permitted material does not reconcile these figures. Neither figure is imposed as a mandatory answer in the binary transaction items.

Sf6ab759d9134 gives June 22, 1922, whereas the later accounting discussion and 1943 order use June 2, 1922. The exact day is not settled. The material distinction is the earlier 1922 mortgage versus the 1931 mortgage.

reference_uncertainties.issue: Substantive identity of the mortgage indebtedness
reference_uncertainties.detail: The original and later deeds have differently named mortgagees. The latter contains a repayment recital, while the 1943 judge found the mortgagees effectively identical as against the debtors. Whether the later transaction was a sufficiently independent advance or continued the earlier indebtedness is not conclusively established.

reference_uncertainties.issue: Income-tax timing and applicable qualification test
reference_uncertainties.detail: The record distinguishes salary deductions, the tax year 1931–32, an assessment form dated 1933, the mortgage date, the application date and the suit date. The 1939 court applied the 1934 Act; the 1943 court made findings under the 1940 Act; the High Court used a different statutory rationale. The withheld target court's treatment remains unavailable.

reference_uncertainties.issue: Statutory scope of the earlier accounting period
reference_uncertainties.detail: Section 8 directs calculation under sections 9 and 10, and section 8(3) protects decree findings subject to inconsistency with section 9. The operative texts of sections 9 and 10 are unavailable. The record therefore cannot establish a definitive statutory rule requiring or prohibiting recalculation from 1922.

S98c21090d1c5 reports the High Court's property-only recovery construction under section 21 of the 1940 Act. The operative section 21 text is not supplied. The interpretation can be accurately attributed to that court but cannot be independently reconstructed or treated as a withheld target-court holding.

reference_uncertainties.issue: Legal effect of the accounting objection's procedural history
reference_uncertainties.detail: The decree-holders did not contest the 1922 starting point in their original objection petition and did not raise it before the High Court. Those historical facts do not by themselves establish waiver, estoppel, res judicata or a bar on further appellate argument. The necessary further appellate reasoning is withheld.

The 1943 court reported full discharge, and the High Court rejected the recorded debt-relief objection. The eventual treatment of the accounting issue, any modification of those findings and the final amount legally enforceable cannot be established from the permitted excerpts.

reference_limitations: This is a source-only model proposal for the design of a reference annotation, not audited human gold, legal certification or an experimental result.

The replacement contains 40 independently assessable, equally weighted binary criteria. Each proposed item has one principal historical relation, statutory obligation, attributed determination or specific supported unresolved question. Mandatory constraints preserve necessary actor, property, transaction, timing, stage, polarity and condition bindings.
Equal weight applies once per proposed item. Shared old_item_ids identify provenance and do not generate additional scoring weight.
No evaluated reports, method identities, grades, experimental scores or target outcomes were consulted or inferred.

The sources are published judgment excerpts rather than original transaction documents, tax records, account books or complete evidentiary transcripts. Reporting a recorded finding does not certify its factual correctness.
The full operative texts of sections 9, 10 and 21 of the 1940 Act are unavailable. Statutory analysis is limited to supplied law and explicitly attributed descriptions in the case excerpts.
The further appellate court's full arguments, reasoning, holdings and disposition are withheld. No proposed item requires acceptance or rejection of the 1943 or High Court conclusions by that court.

An OPEN item is satisfied by identifying its particular supported unresolved question and relevant distinguishing conditions. It does not require a speculative outcome, unsupported statutory application or a generic disclaimer detached from the issue.
No definitive 1922-versus-1931 accounting rule, independently verified zero balance, or ultimate procedural bar is imposed.

The original reference's mechanical quotation mismatches were addressed using exact substrings of the supplied originals. Literal formatting defects were not treated as proof that the associated substantive claims were false.

The proposal retains material adverse positions, statutory gateways, competing time references, mortgage and creditor relationships, hearing evidence, the 1939 and 1943 determinations, the High Court's reported reasoning and the independent substantive and procedural uncertainties. Incidental figures, dates, citation details and unconnected statutes receive no independent point weight.
